senses.gloss:
Cīpudru designates some substance mentioned in a hymn of the Atharvaveda as of use in healing. The commentator Sāyaṇa reads Cīpadru, and explains the word as a kind of tree. This interpretation is supported by the fact that the kauśika sūtra refers to the employment of splinters of palāśa wood in the ritual application of this hymn. Whitney suggests that the form of the word should be Cīpuḍu.
Foot notes vi. 127, 2.

Cf. Bloomfield, Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 350-352; Atharvaveda, 62; Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 386. The text of Roth and Whitney reads by error śīpudru.
